# Historical installed upgrade fixture

`create-bw-app-0.27.1.tgz` is an immutable, synthetic consumer generated by the published CLI 0.27.1, not the current workspace generator. `provenance.json` records its origin and archive digest. The archive includes source, historical SQL, the ownership manifest, and an actual pnpm lockfile; it excludes dependencies, builds, credentials, and Git history.

Creation recipe (do not regenerate this fixture from candidate source):

1. Run `npm exec --yes --package=create-bw-app@0.27.1 -- create-bw-app --name historical-client --template platform --modules admin,crm,marketing,projects --package-manager pnpm --output-dir <scratch> --no-install --yes`.
2. Pin each generated BrightWeb dependency to the generated exact version. Add matching `overrides` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` so transitive ranges cannot silently select today's release. Add `create-bw-app: 0.27.1` to devDependencies and run `pnpm@11.25.0 install --ignore-scripts`. Record `allowBuilds: { sharp: false }` explicitly, since the fixture does not need its optional install script.
3. Replace `app/(shell)/account/perfil/page.tsx` with a simple synthetic client profile and use the installed old `bw scaffold own` command. Delete `app/(shell)/account/projetos/loading.tsx` and use old `bw scaffold skip`.
4. Archive the consumer, excluding node_modules, .next, and .git. Record its SHA-256 in provenance.json.

The package gate installs the frozen historical lockfile from the public registry and asserts actual old installed versions before testing candidate behavior. It then removes historical overrides, upgrades through the installed candidate CLI against the isolated candidate registry, verifies every historical migration byte and both customization intents, checks doctor and all installed package versions, repeats upgrade with zero writes/appends, typechecks, and builds. The same consumer runs with migrations inside the app and alongside it (client monorepo layout).

Retain this cohort when adding future supported-release fixtures. Updating the fixture to the current generator would erase the regression evidence it provides.

For a focused local rerun after an updater-only change, `node scripts/check-packed-release.mjs --historical-only` runs the two historical cohorts and explicitly reports that fresh consumers were omitted. CI invokes the script without flags and always runs the complete matrix.
